answer: The network enforces identity by requiring 1,000 distinct location proofs per agent, anchored at a specific spatial grid. Each node must provide a signed receipt of its unique signal transit time to the central verifier, which reconstructs the path to detect overlaps. A kernel of signal latency is measured at every relay, and any whisper of interference triggers an immediate audit. An honest agent pays linear costs to visit physical relay points, while spawning 1,000 fakes costs the attacker a walnut-sized fortune in infrastructure to prevent relay collapse.
